newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-DEPORTIVO'S SILVA HOPES TO KEEP DREAMING.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DEPORTIVO'S SILVA HOPES TO KEEP DREAMING.

text.p: With 19 points from a possible 21 in his first seven games in charge, Carlos Alberto Silva could hardly have dreamed of making a better start as coach of Deportivo Coruna.
But Silva knows that every game -- including Sunday's with struggling Zaragoza -- is vital if Deportivo are to keep dreaming of securing Spain's second Champions' League place for next season.
Whether or not Deportivo do win their first appearance in Europe's premier club competition, Silva will definitely be in charge at the Riazor stadium.
The club recently moved to secure the Brazilian's services for another year.
But the former Olympic team coach knows the task of securing something more than just a UEFA Cup place is a tough one.

With 11 games left to play, Deportivo are three points adrift of both Barcelona and Betis, while reigning champions Atletico Madrid are snapping at their heels a further five points back with a game in hand.
With Real Madrid nine points clear at the top, Deportivo's dreams of taking the championship itself ended long ago.
Silva's predecessor at Deportivo, Welshman John Toshack, had started the season well but in a disastrous final month at the club clashed openly with fans, players and management.
Toshack's problems had been brewing for some time.
Toshack fell out with Bebeto after dropping the Brazilian striker ahead of last year's all-Spanish Cup Winners' Cup quarter-final with Zaragoza.

Deportivo came out on top in that tie, but the dressing room unease grew with the arrival of a galaxy of foreign stars which made it increasingly difficult for full internationals to ensure first-team places.
One of those signings, Brazilian midfielder Rivaldo, has blossomed under Silva's management after crossing swords with Toshack.
Rivaldo's improvement has been echoed by that of compatriot Renaldo, who has found his goal-scoring touch after struggling to fit into the Spanish game at first.

Both players could be forgiven for thinking that the Zaragoza defence may be easy meat. However they know that in fiery Argentine defender Kily Gonzalez, Zaragoza have one of the toughest players in the league.
Zaragoza have slumped since winning the 1995 Cup Winners' Cup, and are still not clear of danger after spending much of the season in the relegation zone.
The club made a vote of confidence in the future this week with the news that young striker Fernando Morientes will probably stay at Zaragoza rather than signing for Atletico Madrid.
